excluded_metadata_sites.reason: compound/ambiguous Dream Island West (Casey Islands) site
Joubin Islands is a multi-island aggregate rather than a single comparable island
Cape Monaco is an Anvers Island cape, not an island
Anvers Island South West is a main-island site, not a discrete small island

species_abundance.rule: use numeric nest/breeding-pair count or explicit absence independently for each species; no requirement that all sympatric species were counted in the same year
outputs: log ratio where both endpoints positive

community_composition.rule: require every APBP-known focal breeder at the site to have a numeric nest count or explicit absence that year; non-breeders are structural zeros

primary_hypotheses.N1_nonuniform_reassembly: Regional environmental change does not yield uniform species replacement across local breeding patches; true small islands may lose Adelie abundance without gentoo replacement while the Biscoe Point benchmark undergoes Adelie-to-gentoo replacement.
primary_hypotheses.N2_island_vacancy: At true islands that are Adelie-dominated and lack gentoo breeding membership, decline can reduce total colony abundance without a compensatory shift toward the gentoo functional phenotype.
primary_hypotheses.N3_alternative_replacement: Dream Island provides a distinct possible Adelie-to-chinstrap reassembly pathway, testing whether replacement depends on resident/colonizing species identity rather than warming alone.
primary_hypotheses.N4_shared_forcing_local_outcomes: If nearby breeding sites share regional marine forcing but differ in geomorphology and breeding habitat, abundance trajectories should be only partially synchronous and local extirpation/replacement states should differ among sites.

interpretation_boundaries: The primary island set was frozen from site metadata before opening expanded-network abundance outcomes.
Do not label absence from a year as zero unless APBP records explicit absence.
Do not infer competitive displacement from reciprocal abundance changes without a separate interaction analysis.
Biscoe Point is not a true small island and must remain a benchmark rather than being pooled as an island replicate.
Community-weighted morphology uses fixed species centroids and represents assembly-driven functional change, not historical trait evolution.
